newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BZ's Visions to diversify, German pharma bought.
newsitem.headline: BZ's Visions to diversify, German pharma bought.

text.p: BZ Group Holding's investment trusts will diversify their portfolios in the future and Pharma Vision has already invested some 200 million Swiss francs ($144 million) in a German pharmaceuticals group, BZ Bank's president Martin Ebner said on Friday.

Ebner declined to identify the name of the German company, saying this would be announced in mid-March. The investment has been financed by liquidating some of Pharma Vision's holdings of Roche Holding AG bearer shares.

Despite the higher diversification, the number of participations by the trusts -- Pharma Vision, BK Vision, Gas Vision and Stillhalter Vision -- will remain limited as they want to remain focused on a few high-quality companies, Ebner told a news conference.
Accordingly, the work in the BZ Group will be expanded to include research and brokerage on leading European companies.
Ebner acknowledged that Pharma Vision's divestment of some of its shares in Roche could have contributed to the stock's performance last year.
Firstly because there would have been a supply of Roche shares on the market and secondly because of the effect on the market of seeing Pharma Vision as a seller.
BK Vision has not made any major changes in its participations and Ebner said and there were no current plans to sell off its stake in Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).
While Ebner acknowledged the investment in UBS had been a disappointment, leading to an underperformance of BK Vision in 1996, he said BK Vision could at any time sell its stake and realise a gain.
Ebner was hopeful there would be an improvement at UBS over the next half year, adding that contacts to the bank were good.
Among the alternatives that Ebner said were being considered was swapping the stake in UBS for another bank.
Ebner said he could imagine BK Vision investing in German banks but gave no further details.
BK Vision, the largest single owner in UBS, has been engaged in a lengthy battle with UBS over corporate governance shareholder value and several suits are pending in Swiss courts.
Over the next years Ebner expects an intensification in the debate over how to finance old age pension schemes in Switzerland, similar to the discussion in the United States.

Privatisation of mandatory pension schemes was one alternative that should be studied, including the possibility of allowing private individuals to decide whether the state or private companies should manage their pension funds.
Privatisation would lead to competition, more efficiency and higher returns, he added.
Ebner said the aim of the BZ Group over the next years was to increase public awareness of the opportunities in stock markets.
Ebner expects stock markets to continue to perform strongly in the future, given the low inflationary environment and the opportunities presented by globalisation of markets.
-- Peter Nielsen, Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.384 Swiss Francs)
